RRB Group D Cut Off 2026 Released: Your Gateway to the Next Stage!

The much-awaited Railway Recruitment Board (RRB) Group D Cut Off for 2026 has been officially released, bringing a crucial update for thousands of aspirants! Announced on July 1, 2026, along with the CBT results for CEN 08/2024, these cut-off marks are the minimum scores candidates needed to secure to qualify for the next stage of the recruitment process – the Physical Efficiency Test (PET). If you appeared for the RRB Group D 2026 examination, it's time to check your scores and see if you've made the cut!

Understanding the RRB Group D Cut Off

The RRB Group D Cut Off is not just a number; it's the benchmark set by the Railway Recruitment Board to shortlist eligible candidates for the subsequent selection rounds. These marks are released region-wise and category-wise, ensuring fairness across diverse demographics and competitive landscapes. Candidates who score equal to or above these marks are considered qualified for the PET, bringing them one step closer to securing a coveted position in the Indian Railways.

✅ Official Release: RRB Group D Cut Off 2026 declared on July 1, 2026.

✅ Recruitment Cycle: Pertains to CEN 08/2024 recruitment.

✅ Purpose: Shortlists candidates for the Physical Efficiency Test (PET).

✅ Scope: Released zone-wise and category-wise for 32,438 Level-1 posts.

✅ Availability: Accessible on respective regional RRB official websites.

Key Factors Influencing the RRB Group D Cut Off 2026

Several dynamic factors play a crucial role in determining the RRB Group D cut-off marks each year. Understanding these elements can provide insight into why the cut-off fluctuates across zones and categories.

1. Number of Vacancies
The total number of available posts significantly impacts the cut-off. More vacancies in a particular zone generally lead to a lower cut-off, whereas fewer vacancies intensify competition and push the cut-off higher. For CEN 08/2024, there were 32,438 Level-1 posts.
2. Number of Candidates Appearing
The sheer volume of applicants and the actual number of candidates who appeared for the Computer-Based Test (CBT) directly influence the competitive landscape. A larger applicant pool often results in a higher cut-off. For the 2025-26 cycle, over 1.08 crore candidates applied, with nearly 60 lakh appearing for the CBT.
3. Difficulty Level of the Examination
The complexity of the CBT paper is a critical determinant. If the exam is generally considered difficult, the cut-off tends to be lower, and vice versa. Normalization is applied to adjust for varying difficulty levels across multiple shifts.
4. Candidate's Category
Cut-off marks are released separately for different categories such as Unreserved (UR), Other Backward Classes (OBC), Scheduled Castes (SC), Scheduled Tribes (ST), and Economically Weaker Sections (EWS), reflecting reservation policies.
5. Previous Year Cut-Off Trends
While not a direct determinant, previous years' cut-off marks provide valuable insights into the expected range and help candidates set their target scores for preparation.
How to Check Your RRB Group D Cut Off 2026

Candidates can easily access their zone-wise and category-wise cut-off marks on the official regional RRB websites. Follow these simple steps:

1. Visit Your Regional RRB Website
Navigate to the official website of the Railway Recruitment Board zone you applied for (e.g., rrbcdg.gov.in).
2. Locate the Cut-Off Link
On the homepage, look for the link related to "RRB Group D Cut-Off 2026" or "CEN 08/2024 Result and Cut-Off."
3. Download the PDF
Clicking the link will open a PDF document containing the category-wise and zone-wise cut-off marks.
4. Check Your Marks and Save
Examine the cut-off scores for your specific category and zone. It's advisable to download and save the PDF for future reference.

Remember, the cut-off marks are normalized scores out of 100, crucial for fair evaluation across different exam sessions.

Minimum Qualifying Marks vs. Official Cut Off

It's important to differentiate between the minimum qualifying marks and the official cut-off marks. The Railway Recruitment Board sets minimum qualifying percentages for the CBT: 40% for UR/EWS candidates, 30% for OBC/SC candidates, and 25% for ST candidates. While these are baseline eligibility criteria, the actual cut-off marks for selection are typically much higher and are determined by the factors mentioned above. PwBD candidates receive a 2% relaxation on these minimum marks.

RRB Group D Cut Off 2026: Average Analysis

While the detailed zone-wise cut-offs are available on individual RRB websites, an average analysis of the RRB Group D Cut Off 2026 (for CEN 08/2024) provides a general idea of the trends observed across various zones.

Category Average Cut Off Range (Normalized Score)
UR (Unreserved) 72-79 marks
OBC (Other Backward Classes) Generally 1-2 marks lower than UR
EWS (Economically Weaker Section) 60-75 marks
SC (Scheduled Castes) 66-74 marks
ST (Scheduled Tribes) 58-72 marks

These figures represent general trends, and actual cut-offs vary significantly by zone due to local competition and vacancies. Candidates are strongly advised to check the official PDF for their respective zones.

What's Next: The Physical Efficiency Test (PET)

Candidates who have successfully cleared the RRB Group D Cut Off 2026 are now eligible to appear for the Physical Efficiency Test (PET). This is the second crucial stage in the recruitment process, designed to assess the physical fitness of the candidates. Prepare diligently for this stage to move closer to your dream of joining the Indian Railways.

The release of the RRB Group D Cut Off 2026 marks a significant milestone for all applicants. We wish all qualified candidates the very best for their upcoming PET. Keep an eye on the official RRB websites for further announcements and detailed schedules regarding the next phases of recruitment.
